articles.title: Viral Video Shows BSF Jawan Allegedly Dragging Elderly Father on Road Over Property Dispute
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video from Purvamir village under the Maharajpur police station limits in Kanpur has gone viral, allegedly showing a Border Security Force (BSF) jawan assaulting and dragging his elderly father on a public road during a property dispute.

body.html:
A disturbing video from Purvamir village under the Maharajpur police station limits in Kanpur has gone viral, allegedly showing a Border Security Force (BSF) jawan assaulting and dragging his elderly father on a public road during a property dispute. The authenticity of the viral video has not been independently verified.

According to the victim, Ram Shankar Gupta, a retired Home Guard commander, his middle son, Sarvesh, who serves in the BSF, had been pressuring him to transfer family land into his name. He alleged that whenever he refused, his son assaulted him.

The elderly man claimed he had been visiting the local police station and outpost for the past three days seeking help but had not received any assistance. He also alleged that he feared for his life and said he was rescued only after local residents intervened.

Reports further allege that the accused beat the elderly man with sticks, threw him to the ground, and dragged him along the road. Some reports also claim that the accused's wife, a Uttar Pradesh Police constable, was involved in the assault. However, police have not officially confirmed her involvement.

The video of the incident has been widely circulated on social media, prompting police to take cognisance of the matter. Maharajpur Police Station SHO Rajesh Kumar said that although no formal complaint had been received, preventive action had been taken against the accused based on the viral video, and a police team has been deployed to investigate the incident.

Further investigation is underway.

#Kanpur #UttarPradesh #BSF #ViralVideo #BreakingNews

articles.title: Rat Poison' Capsules at Muharram Procession? Mumbai Police Foil Alleged Plot to Kill 15,000 People
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major tragedy was averted during a Muharram Ashura procession in Mumbai after police arrested a man accused of distributing poisonous capsules disguised as painkillers and immunity boosters.

body.html:
A major tragedy was averted during a Muharram Ashura procession in Mumbai after police arrested a man accused of distributing poisonous capsules disguised as painkillers and immunity boosters.

The accused, identified as Fayyaz Premji, was detained near Rehmatabad Cemetery in Byculla after at least 11 people reportedly fell ill upon consuming the capsules. They were rushed to hospital with symptoms including vomiting and stomach pain, and all are now reported to be out of danger.

Police said the capsules contained zinc phosphide, a highly toxic chemical commonly used in rat poison. Deputy Commissioner of Police Jayant Meena confirmed that the accused had mixed zinc phosphide into the capsules and had no authorisation to distribute them.

During the operation, police seized 14,900 capsules from the accused. Investigators also found that he had allegedly ordered 30,000 empty capsules and 50 kg of zinc phosphide. The seized capsules have been sent for forensic examination.

According to police sources, Premji allegedly confessed that he intended to kill thousands of people participating in the procession and reportedly told investigators he wanted to kill at least 15,000 people.

The alleged plot was foiled after three women volunteers noticed the accused distributing capsules suspiciously. They stopped him, alerted the police, and a public announcement was immediately made asking people not to consume the capsules.

Premji, a BBA graduate with a reported travel history to Iran and Iraq, has been remanded to two days of police custody. A case has been registered at Byculla Police Station under Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for causing hurt by poison with intent to commit an offence.

Police are investigating the accused's motive, possible terror links, and whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy.

#Mumbai #Muharram #Ashura #MumbaiPolice #BreakingNews

articles.title: Road Rage Erupts Between Woman in Skoda and Cab Driver on Delhi Road
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A road rage incident on Palam Road near Dwarka Sector-1 in Delhi has come to light after a video of the confrontation surfaced online, showing a heated altercation between a woman travelling in a Haryana-registered Skoda Rapid and a cab driver in the middle of a busy road.

body.html:
A road rage incident on Palam Road near Dwarka Sector-1 in Delhi has come to light after a video of the confrontation surfaced online, showing a heated altercation between a woman travelling in a Haryana-registered Skoda Rapid and a cab driver in the middle of a busy road.

According to the cab driver, the incident began after the Skoda car allegedly collided with his vehicle. He alleged that the woman and another occupant of the car confronted him, leading to a heated argument that escalated into a public altercation.

The cab driver further alleged that he was verbally abused and physically assaulted during the confrontation. Viral videos of the incident appear to show the woman pushing the cab driver before a police officer intervenes and separates the two parties as onlookers gather at the scene.

The altercation caused a brief commotion on the busy stretch, and the videos have since circulated widely on social media.

Police have taken cognisance of the incident and launched an investigation. Officials are examining the viral footage and other available evidence to establish the sequence of events. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

#Delhi #RoadRage #Dwarka #PalamRoad #BreakingNews

articles.title: SUV Driver Fills ₹6,000 Worth of Fuel, Speeds Away Without Paying in Gurugram
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A CCTV camera captured a dramatic fuel theft at a petrol pump on the Pataudi–Bilaspur Road in Gurugram, where the driver of a black Mahindra Scorpio allegedly filled fuel worth ₹6,000 before speeding away without making the payment.

body.html:
A CCTV camera captured a dramatic fuel theft at a petrol pump on the Pataudi–Bilaspur Road in Gurugram, where the driver of a black Mahindra Scorpio allegedly filled fuel worth ₹6,000 before speeding away without making the payment.

The incident took place at Yash Filling Station, where the SUV pulled up for refuelling. According to the petrol pump owner, the driver asked the attendant to fill the tank and then stepped out of the vehicle, appearing to behave normally while keeping an eye on the surroundings.

As soon as the fuel dispenser reached ₹6,000 and the tank was full, the driver quickly got back into the vehicle and sped away before the attendant could remove the nozzle or collect the payment.

The sudden escape pulled the fuel dispenser hose along with the vehicle, snapping the pipe and causing fuel to spill, resulting in additional damage to the petrol pump.

The entire incident was captured on the petrol pump's CCTV cameras. The footage, which has since surfaced online, has been handed over to the police as evidence.

Jagbir Singh Tanwar, owner of Yash Filling Station, lodged a complaint with the local police, alleging that the accused deliberately fled without paying and damaged the dispensing machine in the process.

Police have launched an investigation and are examining the CCTV footage to identify the vehicle's registration number. Officers are also scanning cameras installed along nearby routes to trace the accused's movements.

Further investigation is underway.

#Gurugram #Haryana #CCTV #FuelTheft #BreakingNews

articles.title: Rejected Marriage Proposal Ends in Horror: College Student Stabbed 14 Times in 47 Seconds in Ujjain
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 19-year-old college student was allegedly stabbed 14 times in just 47 seconds by a man who reportedly wanted to marry her after she rejected his advances in Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain on Friday. The accused was arrested within three hours of the attack.

body.html:
A 19-year-old college student was allegedly stabbed 14 times in just 47 seconds by a man who reportedly wanted to marry her after she rejected his advances in Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain on Friday. The accused was arrested within three hours of the attack.

The survivor, Pooja alias Gungun, a first-year B.A. student from Bapu Nagar, worked as a computer operator at a pharmacy in Dawa Bazar. According to police, she was on her way to work at around 12:45 pm when 21-year-old Sunil Jaroliya allegedly intercepted her near Madhav Club.

Police said the accused briefly spoke to the woman before attacking her with a knife after she refused to talk to him. She sustained multiple grievous injuries to her abdomen, neck and hands and was initially taken to the district hospital before being shifted to Patidar Hospital, where she remains in critical condition.

The attack created panic in the busy market, with bystanders rushing to help the injured woman.

During interrogation, the accused allegedly told police that he and Pooja had become friends on Instagram nearly four years ago. He claimed he was upset because she had stopped answering his calls over the past 10 days and that her mother was opposed to their alleged relationship.

Ujjain Superintendent of Police Pradeep Sharma said the accused had allegedly been harassing the young woman, who no longer wished to communicate with him. After the attack, he attempted to flee but fractured his leg while jumping over a wall. He is currently undergoing treatment and will be produced before a court after interrogation.

Police have registered a case and are continuing their investigation.

#Ujjain #MadhyaPradesh #CrimeNews #BreakingNews

articles.title: Man Allegedly Learnt Murder Techniques Online Before Killing Family of Four in Telangana
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A property dispute, unpaid debts, and personal revenge allegedly led to the brutal murder of a family of four in Telangana's Nalgonda district, with police claiming the main accused watched online videos to learn how to commit the crime and avoid detection.

body.html:
A property dispute, unpaid debts, and personal revenge allegedly led to the brutal murder of a family of four in Telangana's Nalgonda district, with police claiming the main accused watched online videos to learn how to commit the crime and avoid detection.

Police cracked the case within four days after the decomposed bodies of Mohammed Sultan, his wife Haseena, son Mujammil, and daughter Afsara were recovered from their locked house on June 22. According to investigators, the murders took place around four days earlier, and the bodies had been wrapped in bedsheets while the house was locked from the outside to delay discovery.

Nalgonda Superintendent of Police Sharath Chandra Pawar said the conspiracy was driven by a property worth over ₹2 crore, unpaid debts, and longstanding family disputes.

According to police, the main accused, Syed Aslam, a Hyderabad-based car driver, was facing financial difficulties due to mounting loans. Investigators said he had earlier borrowed ₹1 lakh from Haseena and later sought another ₹1 lakh loan to purchase a new car. After she allegedly refused and mocked him for not repaying the earlier loan with interest, Aslam allegedly decided to target the family. Police also said he had previously attempted to steal property documents from the house but failed.

Investigators further alleged that Aslam's wife, Tabassum, also held a grudge against Haseena over an earlier family dispute and encouraged him to target the house.

Police said Aslam allegedly watched online videos to learn how to carry out the murders before reaching the family's house in the early hours of June 19. He allegedly stabbed Haseena first before attacking Mohammed Sultan and their two children.

According to the post-mortem report, Sultan suffered six stab wounds, Haseena seven, daughter Afsara nine, and son Mujammil 16. Police suspect Mujammil tried to resist the attack, while Afsara allegedly attempted to hide under a bed before she was dragged out and killed.

After the murders, the accused allegedly fled with cash, gold, and property documents. Police said the stolen jewellery was later pledged for ₹5.30 lakh.

During the investigation, police recovered ₹3 lakh in cash, stolen gold, the murder weapons, blood-stained clothes, mobile phones, and the vehicle allegedly used in the crime.

Four accused — Syed Aslam, Tabassum, Mohammed Sohail, and Hemant Kumar — have been arrested. Two others, who allegedly assisted before and after the murders, remain absconding, and efforts are underway to trace them.

#Telangana #Nalgonda #CrimeNews #BreakingNews #FamilyMurder

articles.title: Rejected Lover Allegedly Kidnaps Woman, Stabs Her in Moving Car Before Dying in Petrol Bomb Blast
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking development in the Tumakuru petrol bomb case, police have alleged that a man kidnapped his former girlfriend, stabbed her inside a moving car, and then detonated a petrol bomb, killing himself.

body.html:
In a shocking development in the Tumakuru petrol bomb case, police have alleged that a man kidnapped his former girlfriend, stabbed her inside a moving car, and then detonated a petrol bomb, killing himself. The woman escaped with serious injuries after jumping out of the vehicle moments before the explosion.

The deceased has been identified as Nagendra, an unemployed man from Hebbul village in Ankola taluk, Uttara Kannada district. The survivor, Ramya (23), is an OT technician at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital in Bengaluru and hails from a neighbouring village in Ankola.

According to police, the two had been in a relationship for the past six years after meeting during their college days. Investigators said Nagendra had recently begun allegedly harassing Ramya and pressuring her to marry him. She reportedly ended the relationship, blocked his phone number, and was living in a rented house in Bhyrasandra Bhovi Colony in Bengaluru.

Police said Nagendra travelled from Ankola to Bengaluru on Thursday morning and allegedly confronted Ramya at her residence around 7 am. When her friend intervened, he allegedly threatened to kill her as well before forcing Ramya into a pre-booked Uber cab and driving towards Ankola. Following the incident, Ramya's friend lodged a kidnapping complaint at Siddapura Police Station.

According to the investigation, Nagendra allegedly threatened Ramya throughout the journey, showed her a petrol bomb he had brought with him, and repeatedly threatened to kill her before taking his own life.

When the cab reached Jogihalli near Sira taluk in Tumakuru district, Nagendra allegedly stabbed Ramya multiple times on her head and hand. After witnessing the attack and noticing the petrol bomb, the cab driver stopped the vehicle on the roadside and fled for safety, police said.

Despite suffering serious injuries, Ramya reportedly managed to unlock the car door and jump out just before Nagendra allegedly detonated the petrol bomb. The vehicle was immediately engulfed in flames, and Nagendra died inside the burning car.

Police rushed to the scene after receiving information about the burning vehicle. A team led by Tumakuru Superintendent of Police Ashok conducted an inspection. Preliminary findings indicate that Nagendra had brought the petrol bomb and detonated it himself. Police are recording statements from the injured woman and the cab driver as part of the ongoing investigation.

The explosion briefly disrupted traffic on the highway. Further investigation is underway.

#Tumakuru #Karnataka #CrimeNews #BreakingNews

articles.title: Shopkeeper Allegedly Beaten for Refusing Credit in Meerut
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A confectionery shopkeeper was allegedly assaulted after refusing to provide goods on credit to a group of individuals in Meerut.

body.html:
A confectionery shopkeeper was allegedly assaulted after refusing to provide goods on credit to a group of individuals in Meerut.

According to reports, the accused entered the shop, abused the shopkeeper, threatened to kill him, and allegedly assaulted him after he refused to extend credit. During the incident, the shopkeeper was seen pleading with folded hands, asking the group to stop, but the assault allegedly continued.

The entire incident was captured on the shop's CCTV camera, and the video has since gone viral on social media.

Police have launched an investigation and are examining the CCTV footage to identify those involved and take appropriate legal action.

Further investigation is underway.

#Meerut #UttarPradesh #CCTV #BreakingNews #CrimeNews

articles.title: School Van Door Flies Open, Children Thrown Onto Bengaluru Road; Driver Booked
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking CCTV video has surfaced showing five schoolchildren falling onto the road after the rear door of a moving private school van allegedly flew open in Bengaluru's KR Puram area on Thursday.

body.html:
A shocking CCTV video has surfaced showing five schoolchildren falling onto the road after the rear door of a moving private school van allegedly flew open in Bengaluru's KR Puram area on Thursday.

The incident occurred in Gayatri Layout and was captured by a CCTV camera installed in the locality. The footage shows the van's rear door suddenly opening while the vehicle was in motion, causing the children to fall onto the road.

Fortunately, there was no traffic immediately behind the van, averting what could have been a major tragedy.

According to police, all five children escaped with minor scrapes and bruises.

Based on the CCTV footage, Traffic Police seized the vehicle and registered an FIR against the driver at KR Puram Police Station.

Police are investigating the exact cause of the incident, including whether it was due to driver negligence, poor vehicle maintenance, or the impact of a pothole, as claimed by some witnesses.

Further investigation is underway.

#Bengaluru #KRPuram #SchoolVan #CCTV #BreakingNews

articles.title: Viral 'Anganwadi Abuse' Video Takes Shocking Twist: Woman Seen Assaulting Toddler Was Child's Mother
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A viral video recorded in Nandgaon village, Panvel, on June 25, showing a woman in a red dress allegedly shoving and kicking a two-year-old girl, initially sparked outrage after many believed the accused was an Anganwadi worker.

body.html:
A viral video recorded in Nandgaon village, Panvel, on June 25, showing a woman in a red dress allegedly shoving and kicking a two-year-old girl, initially sparked outrage after many believed the accused was an Anganwadi worker.

However, Maharashtra Women and Child Development Minister Aditi Sunil Tatkare clarified on June 26 that the woman seen in the video was the child's mother, not an Anganwadi worker. According to the minister, the mother allegedly assaulted the child out of frustration after the toddler refused to enter the Anganwadi centre.

The video, which circulated widely on social media, shows the child being pushed and kicked, causing her to tumble down concrete steps outside the centre.

Following the incident, police registered a case under relevant child protection laws. The mother was counselled and expressed regret over her actions. The matter has also been referred to the Child Welfare Committee for further action.

The incident has reignited concerns over corporal punishment and highlighted the risks of drawing conclusions from viral videos before official verification.

Authorities have urged the public not to circulate the video further to protect the identity and privacy of the minor victim.

#Panvel #Maharashtra #ChildAbuse #ViralVideo #BreakingNews
